mechanism_narrative: The latest weekly rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from their four-week lows signals restored commuting and out-of-home routines that lift discretionary retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -16.0 to -9.0 and WORKPLACES rose from -4.9 to 2.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or above their latest weekly levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean above +10 percent indicates renewed essential-trip concentration and precautionary shopping, which crowds out discretionary retail trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 12.1 in t-0w and 11.0 in t-3w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean whenever GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean exceeds +10, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of PARKS and TRANSIT from their four-week lows signals re-engagement with outdoor and public mobility that spills over into nearby retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -45.3 to -36.4 and TRANSIT rose from -16.0 to -9.0 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both improve by more than 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its last 14-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a return-to-office regime, a WORKPLACES weekly mean at or above zero sustains weekday commuter traffic and after-work retail spending, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES turned positive at 2.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES weekly mean is at or above zero for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Summer vacation season reduces RESIDENTIAL time below 8 percent, and lower residential time releases household members into retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 to 6.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 8.0 and RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its last 7-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of GROCERY_PHARM above +10 and RESIDENTIAL above +6 keeps households in a home-centric caution mode, suppressing discretionary retail and driving RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean > 10.0 and RESIDENTIAL weekly mean > 6.0
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean when both GROCERY_PHARM > 10 and RESIDENTIAL > 6, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT weekly mean below -15 percent signals active mobility restrictions or strong avoidance of public transport, which reduces trips to retail and recreation and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean whenever TRANSIT weekly mean is below -15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 2 points, commuting and out-of-home routines displace home time and raise retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change > +5.0 points and RESIDENTIAL week-on-week change < -2.0 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -4.9 to 2.1 and RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 to 6.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises >5 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL falls >2 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its last 7-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
